sentences.text:
The petitioners being accused Nos. 2 to 4 are seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them in Crime No.15/2022 of Gowribidanuru police station, pending before the learned Principal Civil Judge, (Jr.Dn) & JMFC Court, Gowribidanur, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code ( for short 'IPC') and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (for short 'DP').
NC: 2024:KHC:50767 2.

entities.text: Principal Civil Judge, (Jr.Dn) & JMFC Court, Gowribidanur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that, respondent No.2 as informant filed the first information with respondent No.1-police against accused Nos. 1 to 4.
Accused No.1 is the husband, accused Nos. 2 and 3 are the in-laws and accused No.4 is the sister-in-law of respondent No.2.
It is alleged that respondent No.2 and accused No.1 married on 23.07.2020 and thereafter, respondent No.2 started residing in her matrimonial house along with the accused.
After sometime, accused Nos. 1 to 4 started demanding additional dowry of Rs.5,00,000/- and a two-wheeler, and in that regard, they used to ill-treat respondent No.2 both physically and mentally.
There was a panchayath in the family and inspite of that, the accused is said to have treated respondent No.2 with cruelty, criminally intimidated and abused her in filthy language.
Accordingly, the police have registered the case in Crime No.15/2022 for the above said offences and took up the investigation.

sentences.text: 3. Heard Smt. Mamatha M R, learned counsel for the petitioners, Smt. Rashmi Jadhav, learned Additional SPP for NC: 2024:KHC:50767 respondent No.1 and Sri. Subash Chandra Bose, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the materials on records.

4. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the Petitioners have made out any grounds to allow the petition and to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 5.
Respondent No.2 has filed the first information against accused Nos. 1 to 4, making specific allegations.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2 has produced copies of the statement of accused Nos. 1 and respondent No.2 much before registration of the present complaint, where similar allegations are made.
It is stated that, at the intervention of the elders, the dispute was amicably settled.

There is reference to legal notice issued by accused No.1.
NC: 2024:KHC:50767 6.

Learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that, the investigation by the Investigating Officer is almost complete, and by that time, the interim order of stay was granted by this Court and therefore, charge sheet could not be filed.
There are prima facie materials to suggest commission of the offence by accused Nos. 1 to 4.
The Investigating Officer may investigate into the matter and file the final report.
Under such circumstances, I am of the opinion that the petitioners are not entitled for any relief at this stage.

7. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the Negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
In view of disposal of the main petition, pending IA No.1 of 2022 stands disposed of.

Sd/-
